info.name: 48Date Backend API
info.description:
# 48Date Backend API

REST API for the **48Date** dating app — NestJS 11 (ESM) · PostgreSQL 16 + Prisma 7 · Redis 7 · JWT.

---

## How this collection is organised

Two root folders:

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| **USER** | All **51 implemented endpoints**, consumed by the Flutter app. Serialised `A-01.1` → `SS-06`. |
| **ADMIN** | **Empty placeholder.** No admin endpoints exist in the codebase yet — see that folder's description for the verified details. |

### Reading the serials

Each folder has its own letter prefix, and requests are numbered **01..n within that folder** in integration order:

| Folder | Prefix | Count |
|---|---|---|
| 01 · Auth | `A` | 7 |
| 02 · Profile & Media | `P` | 5 |
| 03 · Discovery | `D` | 5 |
| 04 · Matches | `M` | 2 |
| 05 · Chat (REST) | `C` | 2 |
| 06 · Games | `G` | 4 |
| 07 · Dates | `DT` | 11 |
| 08 · Trust Score | `T` | 2 |
| 09 · Safety | `S` | 5 |
| 10 · Subscriptions | `SB` | 3 |
| 11 · Success Stories | `SS` | 6 |

The **folders themselves** are numbered `01` → `11` in the order you should integrate them: finish Auth before Profile, Profile before Discovery, and so on. Within a folder, a lower number is either a dependency of, or independent from, what follows — so `A-01.1` has no prerequisites at all, while `SS-06` assumes most of the collection already works.

Cross-references in request descriptions use these serials, so "run after **A-02**" always points at exactly one request.

Auth is the one folder with a split serial: **A-01.1 Login** and **A-01.2 Google login** are two alternative ways to start the same flow, so they share step 1.

---

## Setup

1. Start the API: `docker compose up -d postgres redis && npm run start:dev`
2. Set the `baseUrl` variable if you are not on `http://localhost:3000`.
3. Run **A-01.1 Login or sign-up** → **A-02 Verify OTP** → you are authenticated.
4. If the response says `nextStep: "PROFILE_SETUP"`, run **A-03 Verify user information** to finish onboarding.

**Dev OTP is always `123456`.**

### Variables are captured for you

Every request that returns an id writes it into a collection variable, so the folders are runnable top-to-bottom without hand-editing anything:

`userPhone` · `userEmail` · `accessToken` · `refreshToken` · `userId` · `imageUrl` · `targetUserId` · `matchId` · `conversationId` · `gameId` · `questionId` · `sessionId` · `datePlanId` · `storyId` · `commentId`

Authentication is set **collection-wide** to `Bearer {{accessToken}}`; public endpoints individually override it to *No Auth*.

> **There is no register endpoint and no passwords.** `POST /auth/login` finds *or creates* the account for whatever phone/email you send, and an OTP is required on **every** login — not only the first one. Re-running **A-01.1** as many times as you like is therefore always safe; it never returns a conflict.

> **Trying the first-time onboarding path:** set `{{userPhone}}` to `{{onboardingPhone}}` (`+8801811000008`). That account is seeded with a completely blank profile, so A-02 comes back with `isUserVerified: false` and **A-03** has real work to do. `npm run db:seed` resets it to blank again.

---

## Response envelope

Every endpoint — success or failure — returns the same shape:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Operation successful", "messages": [], "data": { } }
```

```json
{ "success": false, "message": "Validation failed", "messages": ["phone must be ..."], "statusCode": 400 }
```

`messages` carries the full list of validation errors; `message` is the first one, suitable for a toast.

---

## Chat is WebSocket-only for sending

The two REST endpoints in folder **05** only *read*. Sending happens over Socket.IO on the same origin as `baseUrl`, authenticated by passing the JWT in the handshake.

| Direction | Event | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| → emit | `joinRoom` | `{ conversationId }` |
| → emit | `sendMessage` | `{ conversationId, content, type? }` — type = TEXT \| IMAGE \| DATE_INVITE \| SYSTEM |
| → emit | `typing` | `{ conversationId, isTyping }` |
| ← listen | `newMessage` | the saved message |
| ← listen | `typing` | `{ userId, isTyping }` |

Postman's WebSocket request type can drive these, but it is not part of this collection.

---

## Known gaps

Behaviour verified against the running server — worth knowing before you integrate:

- **No admin API at all.** See the ADMIN folder.
- **`POST /auth/request-otp` and `GET /auth/me` do not exist** despite older docs listing them. Registration and login already return tokens and the user object, and `GET /users/profile` (**P-03**) replaces `/auth/me`.
- **Google login does not verify the token signature** — it only base64-decodes the payload.
- **Mapbox place search returns `[]`** unless `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` is set.
- **The RevenueCat webhook skips auth entirely** when `REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset.
- Twilio / SMTP / FCM / R2 all **fall back to console logging or local disk** when their env vars are absent, so flows succeed locally without any third-party account.

item.name: USER
item.description:
Everything the Flutter user app consumes — **all 51 implemented endpoints** live here.

Serials run **A-01.1 → SS-06 in integration order**: each folder assumes the ones above it already work. Follow them top to bottom and the collection is runnable end to end without editing variables by hand, because each request captures the ids the next one needs.

Hard dependencies worth knowing:
- Everything after **A-02** needs an `accessToken` — that is the request which issues one.
- **A-03** is only needed while `isUserVerified` is `false`; A-02 tells you via `nextStep`.
- Folders **05, 06, 07** all need a `matchId` from **D-05** / **M-01**, which needs two users who liked each other.
- **DT-10** (rating) requires the date to be `COMPLETED` via **DT-09**.

---

## Getting to a match (needed for folders 04–07)

A match needs **two accounts that both liked each other**, so a single run of this collection cannot produce one. The seeded database already ships with two matches for the default account, which is why folders 04–07 work out of the box — run `npm run db:seed` and they are there.

To build one by hand from empty accounts instead:

1. Clear `userPhone`, `userEmail`, `accessToken` and `userId`, then run **A-01.1 → A-02 → A-03**. The pre-request script invents a fresh phone and login creates the account. Note the `userId` — call this **User A**.
2. Clear those four variables again and repeat **A-01.1 → A-02 → A-03**. This is **User B**.
3. As User B, run **D-05 Swipe** with `targetUserId` set to User A's id and `action: LIKE`.
4. Log back in as User A (**A-01.1 → A-02** with A's phone), then run **D-05** with `targetUserId` = User B's id and `action: LIKE`.
5. The second like returns `isMatch: true` and captures `matchId` automatically. Folders **04–07** are now runnable.

Both accounts need **A-03** completed — discovery only returns candidates whose `isUserVerified` is `true`.

The id variables ship with the value `REPLACE_ME` so that an unset id fails loudly with a clear 404 rather than silently collapsing to a different route.

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description:
Login, OTP verification, onboarding and token lifecycle.

**There is no register endpoint.** `POST /auth/login` creates the account for any phone or email it has not seen before, and Google sign-in does the same for any new Google address.

**Start here:** A-01.1 → A-02 → A-03. That chain fills `{{accessToken}}`, which every other folder depends on. Tokens are captured into collection variables automatically.

### The flow
| Step | Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A-01.1 | `POST /auth/login` | Finds or creates the account, always sends an OTP. **No tokens.** |
| A-01.2 | `POST /auth/google` | Finds or creates the account from a Google ID token. Issues tokens immediately — no OTP. |
| A-01.3 | `POST /auth/resend-otp` | Re-sends the OTP for an existing account. Refuses inside a 30-second cooldown (**429**). |
| A-02 | `POST /auth/verify-otp` | Issues `accessToken` + `refreshToken`. Sets `isPhoneVerified` or `isEmailVerified`. |
| A-03 | `POST /auth/verify-user-information` | Sent only when `isUserVerified` is `false`. Writes the whole profile and flips `isUserVerified` to `true`. |

`nextStep` tells the app where to go after A-02 / A-01.2: `PROFILE_SETUP` → send A-03, `MAIN_APP` → onboarding is already done.

An OTP is required on **every** login, not just the first one.

OTP in development is always the dummy code `123456` (see `DUMMY_OTP` in `auth.service.ts`). Real Twilio Verify is used only when the `TWILIO_*` env vars are set.

**There are no passwords anywhere in this API** — no password field, no password login, and no forgot/reset-password flow. Losing access to the phone or email is the only way to lose the account.

request.description:
Logs in **or signs up** with a phone number. There is no register endpoint and no password.

**Auth:** none.

| Field | Type | Req | Valid values / rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `phone` | string | **yes** | E.164 with country code, e.g. `+8801811000001`. The only field this endpoint takes. |

### What it does
1. A number the server has never seen **creates the account** — the response carries `isNewAccount: true`.
2. An OTP is dispatched **every time**, verified or not. This endpoint never returns tokens.
3. Continue with **A-02 Verify OTP**, which issues the `accessToken` / `refreshToken` pair.

> **Phone is the only login channel.** There is no `channel` field and no email login — email reaches an account only through **A-01.2 Google login**.

### 30-second cooldown
Calling this again within **30 seconds** of the last OTP returns **429** with the seconds remaining in the message and in the standard `Retry-After` header. `data.resendCooldownSeconds` tells the OTP screen how long to disable its resend button. Use **A-01.3 Resend OTP** for the "Didn't get a code?" button.

A brand-new account has never been sent anything, so its first OTP is never held back.

In development (no `TWILIO_*` env vars) the OTP is the fixed code `123456`, echoed back in `data.otp`; the test script saves it to `{{otp}}` so A-02 needs nothing typed in.

Exchanges a Google ID token for a 48Date token pair, creating the account on first use.

**Auth:** none.

request.description:
Re-sends the OTP from **A-01.1** — the "Didn't get a code?" button.

**Auth:** none.

| Field | Type | Req | Valid values / rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `phone` | string | **yes** | E.164 with country code. Must belong to an existing account. |

### How it differs from A-01.1
| | A-01.1 Login | A-01.3 Resend |
|---|---|---|
| Unknown number | **Creates** the account | **404** — resending implies something was sent |
| Cooldown | Applies, except on the very first send for a new account | Always applies |

### The 30-second cooldown
Both this endpoint and **A-01.1** refuse to dispatch another OTP within **30 seconds** of the last one, and answer **429** with the exact seconds remaining:

```
Please wait 18 seconds before requesting another code.
```

The count is in the message so you can render a live countdown, and also in the standard **`Retry-After`** response header. `data.resendCooldownSeconds` on a successful resend tells you how long to disable the button for.

Without this, a user leaning on the resend button burns SMS credit, and anyone can spam a stranger's phone for free.

> A brand-new account created by A-01.1 has never been sent anything, so its first OTP is not held back — the cooldown only starts once something has actually gone out.

request.description:
The one-shot onboarding submission. Send it when A-02 (or A-01.2) came back with `isUserVerified: false` / `nextStep: "PROFILE_SETUP"`.

**Auth:** `Bearer {{accessToken}}`.

### Every field is required
The onboarding screens collect all of it, so a missing field means a screen was skipped. The API names each one in `messages[]` with a sentence you can show the user as-is — one message per field, never the same thing said three ways. A 2xx therefore always means the account is now verified and routed to `MAIN_APP`.

Later edits go through **P-02 Profile setup**, which is a PATCH and accepts any subset.

### The one conditional: location
`lastLocation`, `latitude` and `longitude` are required **only when** `locationPermission` is `WHILE_IN_USE`, `ONE_TIME` or `ALWAYS` — i.e. the device actually handed over a position. Send `locationPermission: "DENIED"` on its own and onboarding still completes, because someone who taps *Deny* on the location screen must still be able to finish.

### Fields
| Field | Type | Required | Valid values / rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lastLocation` | string | if granted | City name, reverse-geocoded by the app. |
| `latitude` | number | if granted | −90 … 90. |
| `longitude` | number | if granted | −180 … 180. |
| `locationPermission` | enum | **yes** | `NOT_ASKED` · `WHILE_IN_USE` · `ONE_TIME` · `ALWAYS` · `DENIED` · `DENIED_FOREVER` |
| `username` | string | **yes** | 3–30 chars, letters/numbers/underscores. Unique → `409` if taken. |
| `firstName` | string | **yes** | Non-empty. |
| `lastName` | string | **yes** | Non-empty. |
| `birthDate` | string | **yes** | `YYYY-MM-DD`, must be in the past. |
| `occupation` | string | **yes** | Non-empty free text. |
| `smoker` | enum | **yes** | `NEVER` · `SOMETIMES` · `DAILY` |
| `alcohol` | enum | **yes** | `NEVER` · `SOMETIMES` · `DAILY` |
| `gender` | enum | **yes** | `MALE` · `FEMALE` · `NON_BINARY` · `OTHER` |
| `kids` | enum | **yes** | `HAS_KIDS` · `DOESNT_HAVE_KIDS` · `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` |
| `wantsKids` | boolean | **yes** | |
| `interestedIn` | enum | **yes** | Same values as `gender`. |
| `creativity` | string[] | **yes** | ≥1 of: `ART` · `DESIGN` · `MAKEUP` · `PHOTOGRAPHY` · `SINGING` |
| `sports` | string[] | **yes** | ≥1 of: `RUNNING` · `GYM` · `SOCCER` · `CRICKET` · `TENNIS` · `BASKETBALL` |
| `moviesAndDramas` | string[] | **yes** | ≥1 of: `TV_SHOWS` · `ROMANCE` · `COMEDY` · `K_DRAMA` · `HORROR` · `THRILLER` · `SCI_FI` · `FANTASY` · `ANIME` · `ZOMBIE` |
| `heightCm` | integer | **yes** | 50–250. |
| `weightKg` | integer | **yes** | 20–300. |
| `lookingFor` | enum | **yes** | `REAL_RELATIONSHIP` · `SOMETHING_MEANINGFUL` · `SEE_WHERE_IT_GOES` · `NEW_FRIENDS_FIRST` |
| `images` | object[] | **yes** | 1–6, each `{ url, isMain, sortOrder }`, **exactly one** `isMain: true`. |
| `notificationsEnabled` | boolean | **yes** | |
| `selfieVerificationImageUrl` | string | **yes** | Selfie used for face verification. Stored as `selfieUrl`. |

  "kids": "DOESNT_HAVE_KIDS",  // Required. One of: HAS_KIDS, DOESNT_HAVE_KIDS, PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY (UPPERCASE).

  "sports": ["RUNNING", "GYM"],  // Required. At least one of: RUNNING, GYM, SOCCER, CRICKET, TENNIS, BASKETBALL (UPPERCASE).
  "moviesAndDramas": ["ROMANCE", "K_DRAMA"],  // Required. At least one of: TV_SHOWS, ROMANCE, COMEDY, K_DRAMA, HORROR, THRILLER, SCI_FI, FANTASY, ANIME, ZOMBIE (UPPERCASE).

  ],
  "notificationsEnabled": true,  // Required. Boolean.
  "selfieVerificationImageUrl": "{{selfieUrl}}"  // Required. Selfie used for face verification; stored on the user as selfieUrl.
}

request.description:
Adds or replaces the phone number or email address on the signed-in account.

**Auth:** Bearer.

| Field | Type | Req | Valid values / rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | enum | **yes** | `PHONE` or `EMAIL` — UPPERCASE. |
| `value` | string | **yes** | Validated against `type`: E.164 with country code for `PHONE`, an email address for `EMAIL`. |

Whatever is written lands **unverified** — and replacing an already-verified value resets its flag, because the new one has proven nothing. Confirm it with **P-08** then **P-09**.

### How the two verification flags work
`isPhoneVerified` and `isEmailVerified` are only ever set by the identifier you actually proved:

| You signed up with | Verified on day one | Needs this flow |
|---|---|---|
| Phone (**A-01.1 → A-02**) | `isPhoneVerified` | the email |
| Google (**A-01.2**) | `isEmailVerified` — Google already proved it | the phone |

Neither is set by **A-03 Verify user information**, which is why a freshly onboarded phone user reports `isEmailVerified: false` even after filling in the whole profile.

`isUserVerified` is a separate thing entirely: an **admin-granted trust badge**. No user-facing endpoint sets it.

request.description:
Sends a verification code to the phone or email stored on the account by **P-07**.

**Auth:** Bearer.

| Field | Type | Req | Valid values / rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | enum | **yes** | `PHONE` or `EMAIL` — UPPERCASE. |

### Cooldown
30 seconds, with its own timer — **separate from the login cooldown**, so signing in does not stop you verifying an email you added seconds later. Refusals are **429** with the seconds remaining in the message and in the `Retry-After` header.

### Errors worth knowing
- **400** if nothing of that type is stored yet — add it with **P-07** first.
- **400** if it is already verified; there is nothing to prove.

> Email has no provider wired up (`SMTP_*` is unused), so an email code is always the dev dummy `123456` today. Phone uses Twilio Verify when `TWILIO_*` is set.

request.description:
Returns the candidate feed, filtered by the caller's preferences and excluding anyone already swiped, matched or blocked.

**Auth:** Bearer. No parameters, no body.

Each candidate carries `location.distanceKm` — great-circle distance from **you**, rounded to one decimal. Raw coordinates of other users are never returned; distance is as precise as someone else's position gets.

### How distance filtering behaves
| Your stored coordinates | Result |
|---|---|
| Set | Candidates beyond `maxDistanceKm` (**D-02**) are excluded. Candidates without coordinates are excluded too — an unknown distance cannot satisfy a distance preference. `distanceKm` is a number. |
| Not set | **No distance filtering at all** — you get an unfiltered feed rather than an empty screen. `distanceKm` is `null` on every candidate. |

Set your coordinates with **P-06 Update location**.

The script saves the first candidate's id into `{{targetUserId}}`.

> **Empty feed?** Candidates must have `isUserVerified = true`, and you cannot see yourself. With a single account this always returns `[]` — log a second user in (A-01.1 → A-02) and complete A-03 for them.

> **Seeded demo:** Rafiq Das sits ~190 km from Dhaka. At Ava's default `maxDistanceKm` of 50 he is filtered out; raise it past 200 with **D-02** and he appears. That is the quickest way to see the filter actually working.

item.name: 12 · Realtime (Socket.IO)
item.description:
Chat is **send-over-socket, read-over-REST**. `C-01` and `C-02` only read history — there is no REST endpoint that sends a message. Everything below was verified against a running server.

## Connecting

Postman: **New → WebSocket**, switch the protocol dropdown to **Socket.IO**, and connect to:

```
ws://localhost:3000
```

Default namespace `/`, default Socket.IO path `/socket.io`. Nothing else to configure.

### Auth — pick either, both work

| Method | Where | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Header | Headers tab | `Authorization` = `Bearer <accessToken>` |
| Query param | URL | `ws://localhost:3000?token=<accessToken>` |

Use the `{{accessToken}}` captured by **A-02**. The handshake verifies the JWT; an invalid or missing token **connects and is then immediately disconnected by the server**, so a socket that drops the instant it opens means the token was rejected.

## Events you send

Add these under the **Events** tab of the Socket.IO request (event name + JSON argument).

### `joinRoom`
```json
{ "conversationId": "<uuid>" }
```
Ack: `{ "success": true }` — or `{ "error": "You are not a participant in this conversation" }`.
**You must join before sending**, and you only receive broadcasts for rooms you joined. Use `{{conversationId}}` from **M-01** / **C-01**.

### `sendMessage`
```json
{ "conversationId": "<uuid>", "content": "Hello!", "type": "TEXT" }
```
`type` is optional, defaults to `TEXT`. Valid: `TEXT` · `IMAGE` · `DATE_INVITE` · `SYSTEM` (case-sensitive).

Ack: `{ "success": true, "messageId": "<uuid>" }`

Errors: `{ "error": "Invalid message request" }` (missing `conversationId` or `content`), `{ "error": "Conversation not found" }`, `{ "error": "Unauthorized to send message to this conversation" }`.

The message is persisted, so **C-02** returns it afterwards.

### `typing`
```json
{ "conversationId": "<uuid>", "isTyping": true }
```
No ack. Broadcast to the *other* participants only — never echoed back to you.

## Events you receive

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `newMessage` | the full message: `{ id, conversationId, senderId, type, content, mediaUrl, createdAt }` | someone sends a message to a room you joined |
| `typing` | `{ userId, isTyping }` | the other participant starts/stops typing |
| `gameStarted` | the game session incl. `game.questions[]` | **G-02** opens a session |
| `partnerAnswered` | `{ questionId, userId }` | the partner answered, but **their choice is withheld** until you answer too |
| `roundResult` | `{ questionId, isMatch, answers: [{ userId, selectedOption }] }` | both players answered a question |
| `gameCompleted` | `{ sessionId, compatibility, totalQuestions, matchingAnswers }` | the final question is answered |

Game events are pushed to the match's conversation room, so **join the room first** or you will not see them while using the Games folder.

## Verified transcript

Two clients (Ava and Liam) in one conversation:

```
ava   joinRoom  -> { "success": true }
liam  joinRoom  -> { "success": true }
ava   typing    -> liam receives { "userId": "d6cb56b3-…", "isTyping": true }
ava   sendMessage -> ack { "success": true, "messageId": "a2552cb6-…" }
                     liam receives newMessage { id, senderId, type: "TEXT", content }
```

> ⚠️ **This was broken until recently.** The gateway read `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET` at import time, before `.env` was loaded, so *every* socket connection failed with `secret or public key must be provided`. Fixed by loading `dotenv` first in `main.ts` — if sockets reject a valid token, make sure you are on that build.

item.description:
# ⚠️ No admin endpoints are implemented yet

This folder is an intentionally empty placeholder so the collection structure is ready when the admin API lands. **Nothing has been stubbed or invented here** — adding fake requests would be worse than an empty folder.

## Verified state of the code (as of this collection)

- `src/modules/admin/admin.module.ts` — the controller, service and providers are all **commented out**; the module exports an empty `@Module({})`.
- `AdminModule` is **not imported** into `app.module.ts`, so Nest never registers it.
- `src/modules/admin/types/admin.types.ts` contains only `export {}`.
- The `@Roles()` decorator (`src/common/decorators/roles.decorator.ts`) and `RolesGuard` (`src/common/guards/roles.guard.ts`) both exist but are **applied to zero controllers** — every guarded route in this API uses the plain `JwtAuthGuard`.
- The `Role` enum does contain `ADMIN`, and users carry a `role` field, so the data model is ready.

All 54 routes the server actually maps are user-facing and live under the **USER** folder.

## What the React admin panel will need

These are the gaps implied by features that already exist on the user side — they are **not implemented**, listed only so the work is visible:

- **Moderation queue** — `reports` rows are created by `S-04` with status PENDING and there is currently no way to review, resolve or dismiss them.
- **Success-story approval** — `SS-01` creates stories with status PENDING, and nothing can move them to PUBLISHED, so the public list `SS-02` can never grow.
- **User administration** — suspend/ban, trust-score override, manual verification.
- **Analytics** — signups, matches, dates completed, subscription revenue.

When those endpoints are built, number them **A-01, A-02, …** inside subfolders here, mirroring the USER convention.
